authorship: AI-assisted analytic contribution for ProveIt; repository ownership is not an authorship assignment.
novelty_scope: Contribution classes are relative to the pinned inspected source state, not global priority claims.

claims.title: Finite Bernoulli formula for every harmonic principal part
claims.statement_summary: For a polynomial in generalized harmonic numbers, finite shifted Bernoulli substitution gives every complete principal part at s=1-j.
inputs: Classical Gamma/polygamma asymptotics and Hurwitz-zeta continuation
claims.scope_and_limitations: The finite-part extraction mechanism is classical and extends the source harmonic framework; no new continuation principle is claimed.

claims.title: Injectivity of the centered formal harmonic substitution
claims.statement_summary: The formal substitution of centered harmonic asymptotic series is injective over the complex polynomial ring.
claims.scope_and_limitations: Uses differential algebraic independence of formal series, not arithmetic independence of special numerical constants.

claims.title: Necessary and sufficient centered parity criterion
claims.statement_summary: Regularity at every nonpositive even spectral integer is equivalent to invariance under simultaneous sign reversal of all even-order harmonic tails.
claims.scope_and_limitations: For polynomial numerators with complex coefficients and centered outer shift 1/2; paired ring generators need not be algebraically free.
claims.source_question: Exact Resonant Identities, Q11: answered for the stated polynomial family.

claims.title: Complementary pole lattices and nonentireness
claims.statement_summary: Invariant and anti-invariant numerator parts have complementary possible pole lattices; a nonzero polynomial numerator cannot produce an entire centered Dirichlet function.

claims.title: All centered trigamma-square even moments
claims.statement_summary: Every value at a nonpositive even order is an explicit finite Bernoulli convolution in Q+Q*zeta(3), and equals an ordinary absolutely convergent subtracted sum.
claims.scope_and_limitations: The r=0 value 3*zeta(3) is classical. This single-tail centered family is distinct from the source Dougall-derived weighted squares of shifted trigamma differences.

claims.title: Convergent classical-polylogarithm generator for the moments
claims.statement_summary: The complete even-moment sequence has an even holomorphic exponential generator for |t|<2*pi, with an exact Li_2/Li_3/Li_4 representation.
claims.scope_and_limitations: The displayed classical-polylogarithm branch is first specified for positive real t; the integral formula fixes its holomorphic continuation.

claims.title: Completed all-index cotangent-Stieltjes resolvent
claims.statement_summary: Every Stieltjes index and argument derivative has a finite normalized-polylogarithm order-derivative formula, including the full endpoint polynomial E_p(s).
claims.scope_and_limitations: Nonreal resolvent parameter; finite parts are in the original endpoint coordinate x. The correction is part of the formula.
claims.source_question: Exact Resonant Identities, Q8: rational sector addressed; arbitrary nonpolynomial families remain open.

claims.title: Repeated resolvents and bounded rational closure
claims.statement_summary: Parameter differentiation gives every repeated pole; partial fractions give every rational function of cotangent bounded at infinity and with no real pole.
claims.scope_and_limitations: Ordinary convergence when the repeated-pole order exceeds the argument-derivative order. No closure claim for arbitrary complex powers.

claims.title: Continuous-order transform and exact finite-part conversion
claims.statement_summary: The established Espinosa-Moll generalized polygamma has an entire-order resolvent transform; specialization to nonnegative integers differs from pointwise finite parts by an explicit harmonic endpoint polynomial.
claims.scope_and_limitations: The ordinary integral initially requires Re(v)<1; its explicit transform is entire in v. The special-function definition itself is classical.

claims.title: Compatible continuous and pointwise derivative recurrences
claims.statement_summary: The continuous transform and pointwise finite-part hierarchy satisfy explicit Riccati-based recurrences, with the latter retaining its endpoint term.

claims.title: Balanced Gamma primitive resolvents at every level
claims.statement_summary: Every classically normalized balanced negapolygamma primitive has an ordinary convergent resolvent integral in normalized polylogarithms and order derivatives.
claims.scope_and_limitations: Balanced primitive normalizations and Barnes identities are inherited/classical. No evaluation of every unbalanced Barnes-G product is asserted.
claims.source_question: Exact Resonant Identities, Q9: the specified rational-kernel balanced family is answered.

claims.title: Boundary jump and recovery of Stieltjes functions
claims.statement_summary: Cauchy boundary values recover the Stieltjes density and classical Hurwitz-polylogarithm connection.
claims.scope_and_limitations: Included as an exact inversion and phase check, not as a new Hurwitz functional equation.

claims.title: Nonpositive-index deletion at any position
claims.statement_summary: Every fixed nonpositive index can be eliminated at any depth and position using finite Bernoulli shifts, for arbitrary right-half-plane endpoints and all remaining spectral indices.
claims.scope_and_limitations: Only remaining free indices may be differentiated; transverse derivatives of a fixed eliminated index are not licensed.

claims.title: Canonical gap-polynomial normal form
claims.statement_summary: A word with fixed nonpositive indices has a finite polynomial-coefficient reduction to the surviving free orders; all deletion orders give the same universal coefficient polynomials with an explicit degree budget.
inputs: Polynomial uniqueness on a Zariski-dense finite-interval lattice
claims.scope_and_limitations: Uniqueness is for the specified universal polynomial normal form, not minimal arithmetic depth or analytic interpolation from integer endpoints.

claims.title: Analytic Lerch generator for every zero decoration
claims.statement_summary: All zero blocks around one free order sum to a convergent bivariate generating function through a single entire-order endpoint Lerch difference.
claims.scope_and_limitations: Holomorphic for |t|<2*pi and entire in the free order; a sufficient bivariate domain is |u|,|v|<1/2. No minimal multivariate-free-order kernel is claimed.

claims.title: One-free-order Gamma, polygamma, and Stieltjes consequences
claims.statement_summary: Every one-free-order word and its free-order derivatives reduce finitely to Hurwitz differences, including explicit Gamma and Stieltjes resonant values.

claims.title: Normalized polynomial endpoint primitives and Stieltjes moments
claims.statement_summary: A fully indexed arbitrary-endpoint version of established polynomial Hurwitz integration and Stieltjes coefficient extraction, with the additive normalization fixed.
inputs: Espinosa-Moll, On Some Integrals Involving the Hurwitz Zeta Function: Part 2, Theorem 2.1 and Example 2.2
claims.scope_and_limitations: Not a new integration principle; the existing canonical and classical attribution must be preserved.

claims.title: Elementary polar normalization and source restrictions
claims.statement_summary: The holomorphic remainder R, its exact C-axis, and Euler-plane relation are reproduced to state the new higher-order results consistently.
inputs: Independent Orders and Exact Reductions, Section 3
claims.scope_and_limitations: These analytic identities and the existing cubic classification are not claimed as new here.

claims.title: Every quartic Tornheim direction in three coordinates
claims.statement_summary: All admissible fourth directional derivatives reduce to the diagonal fourth derivative Lambda, a Gamma-series coordinate U, a mixed polylogarithmic coordinate Xi, and ordinary zeta derivatives.
claims.scope_and_limitations: Requires (a+c)(b+c) nonzero. Three is a coordinate count in the named formal relation space, not arithmetic independence.
claims.source_question: Independent Orders Section 7 Question 2 and Cubic Harmonic research problem 4: quartic directional layer answered.

claims.title: Explicit convergent mixed coordinate
claims.statement_summary: Xi=R_AAB(0) is represented by an ordinary absolutely convergent integral of polylogarithmic order derivatives plus a fully explicit elementary correction.
claims.scope_and_limitations: This fixes a convergent representative; it does not evaluate Xi in a prescribed finite standard-constant algebra.

claims.title: The Gamma coordinate used by quartic rays
claims.statement_summary: U=R_AAA(0) is the j=3 specialization of the source boundary-jet theorem involving a convergent logarithmic Gamma remainder series.
inputs: Independent Orders, boundary-germ and boundary-jet theorem
claims.scope_and_limitations: The Gamma moment specialization is explicitly inherited, not a separate new identity claim.

claims.title: Quartic cyclic elimination
claims.statement_summary: Every admissible cyclic quartic combination removes both additional coordinates and all fourth zeta derivatives at -1, leaving one diagonal coordinate and explicit zeta derivatives at 0.
claims.scope_and_limitations: Individual cyclic restrictions require all pairwise sums of the directions to be nonzero.

claims.title: Exact homogeneous kernel and formal dimensions
claims.statement_summary: Under the named symmetry, C-axis and Euler-plane relations, every degree-d freedom has a unique S,Q polynomial form, with dimension floor(d/2)+floor(d^2/4).
inputs: Polynomial divisibility and exact finite-dimensional algebra
claims.scope_and_limitations: Does not impose every known or possible Tornheim functional relation and does not prove numerical period independence.
claims.source_question: Independent Orders higher directional and cancellation questions: formal quotient component answered.

claims.title: All-order cyclic image, factorization, and fifth-order obstruction
claims.statement_summary: The cyclic freedom is ABC times all symmetric degree-(d-2) polynomials; its derivative-order-n dimension is floor((n^2+3)/12). An explicit fifth-order deformation is invisible on the diagonal.
inputs: Holomorphic cyclic cancellation and coordinate-plane divisibility
claims.scope_and_limitations: The fifth-order obstruction concerns inference from the named relations and diagonal data, not an impossibility theorem for additional analytic relations.

open_boundaries: No evaluation of Lambda or Xi in a prescribed finite standard-constant algebra.
No arithmetic independence of Tornheim, harmonic, or Stieltjes coordinates.
No universal closure theorem for arbitrary nonrational cotangent kernels.
No general minimal generating kernel with several independent free harmonic orders.
No transverse differentiation of a fixed eliminated nonpositive index.
No proof or refutation of S6 or revised S8.
